subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient reconnect attempts stay unlimited by default with an opt-in cap for short-lived callers, or should OpenClaw impose a default reconnect ceiling across all clients?
rationale: Both current code and the linked discussion show the code defect, but choosing the default retry policy can affect node-host recovery and exported GatewayClient API behavior.

options.title: Adopt opt-in package-client cap
options.body: Add maxReconnectAttempts to the active package client and wire only short-lived callers that should fail boundedly, keeping node-host unlimited unless explicitly changed.

options.title: Default cap everywhere
options.body: Impose a finite retry ceiling for all GatewayClient users, accepting that existing long-lived node-host deployments may stop recovering automatically after prolonged outages.

options.title: Keep unlimited retries
options.body: Treat endless reconnect as intentional for all GatewayClient users and close the issue only after documenting why short-lived clients should supervise themselves.

recommendation.title: Adopt opt-in package-client cap
recommendation.body: Add maxReconnectAttempts to the active package client and wire only short-lived callers that should fail boundedly, keeping node-host unlimited unless explicitly changed.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently owned the package-client boundary where the durable fix now belongs.
